## Learning Objectives {.unnumbered}

{{< include ../learning_objectives/0648-containers-uv-renv.qmd >}}

## Download the images before you start {.unnumbered}

The image in this chapter builds on the two images
from [Python packages with uv in an image](0640-containers-uv.qmd)
and [R packages with renv in an image](0645-containers-renv.qmd).
Start Docker first (on macOS and Windows, open Docker Desktop),
then download (pull) them before you start:

```bash
docker pull rocker/r-ver:4.6.2
docker pull ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.7
```

## The example project

Many data analyses use Python and R together,
for example a Python script that cleans the data
and an R script that fits a model.
This chapter builds one image with both,
from [docker-uv-renv](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv),
the example project that the rest of this part of the book uses.
Get a copy of it with Git:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv.git
cd docker-uv-renv
```

Its Python packages are listed in `pyproject.toml` and locked in `uv.lock`, as in the uv chapter:

```{.toml}
[project]
name = "docker-uv-renv"
version = "2026.11.13"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = [
    "altair==6.3.0",
    "pandas==3.1.1",
    # Altair charts as images, for PDFs
    "vl-convert-python==1.9.0.post1",
    # Quarto needs these to run Python code
    "ipykernel==7.4.0",
    "nbclient==0.11.0",
    "pyyaml==6.0.3",
]

[tool.uv]
# `uv add` writes an exact version (==)
add-bounds = "exact"
```

Its R packages are listed in `DESCRIPTION` and locked in `renv.lock`, as in the renv chapter:

```{.yaml}
Type: project
Version: 2026.11.13
Description: The R packages this project uses. renv.lock locks them.
Depends:
    dplyr (== 1.2.1),
    ggplot2 (== 4.0.3),
    knitr (== 1.52),
    rmarkdown (== 2.32)
```

Its `reports/` folder has two Quarto reports that make the same table and chart,
`report-python.qmd` with pandas and Altair,
and `report-r.qmd` with dplyr and ggplot2.

## The `Dockerfile`

Here is the project's whole `Dockerfile`:

```{.dockerfile}
# Ubuntu with R. Other versions:
# https://rocker-project.org/images/versioned/r-ver.html
FROM rocker/r-ver:4.6.2

# libuv1-dev: the fs R package needs it (see renv::sysreqs())
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install --yes \
    curl \
    git \
    less \
    libuv1-dev \
    make \
    nano \
    openssh-server

# install quarto
# quarto comes with Typst for PDFs, so no LaTeX.
# dpkg --print-architecture: amd64 or arm64, to match your computer.
RUN curl --location --output quarto.deb \
    https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v1.11.9/quarto-1.11.9-linux-$(dpkg --print-architecture).deb \
  && apt-get install --yes ./quarto.deb \
  && rm quarto.deb

# install python uv
# https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/docker/#installing-uv
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.7 /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/

# The project is mounted over /workspace, so the packages go in /opt
WORKDIR /workspace

# python packages in /opt/venv
ENV UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv
# ssh logins don't see ENV, only /etc/environment
RUN echo "UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=$UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT" >> /etc/environment
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock .python-version ./
# --locked: stop if uv.lock doesn't match pyproject.toml
RUN uv sync --locked

# R packages in /opt/renv/library
RUN echo "RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY=/opt/renv/library" >> /usr/local/lib/R/etc/Renviron.site
COPY renv.lock .Rprofile ./
COPY renv/activate.R renv/
RUN Rscript -e "renv::restore()"

# For linux laptops:
# StrictModes no: sshd wants root to own the key file,
# but on Linux the mounted one is yours
# RUN echo "StrictModes no" > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/container.conf

# -D: stay in the foreground, so the container keeps running
CMD ["/usr/sbin/sshd", "-D"]
```

Most of it comes from the two previous chapters.
It starts from the R image,
because `rocker/r-ver` has no Python:

```bash
docker run --rm rocker/r-ver:4.6.2 bash -c 'command -v python3 || echo "no python3"'
```

```out
no python3
```

That does not matter, because uv installs the Python version in `.python-version`,
as it did on top of Ubuntu.
So the uv lines can be added to the R image unchanged:

- `FROM rocker/r-ver:4.6.2`, the `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY` line,
  the two `COPY` lines for renv and `renv::restore()`
  are the lines from [R packages with renv in an image](0645-containers-renv.qmd).
- `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.7`, `ENV UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv`,
  the `COPY` line for uv and `uv sync --locked`
  are the lines from [Python packages with uv in an image](0640-containers-uv.qmd).
- `WORKDIR /workspace` is in both.

The rest is new:

- The `apt-get` line installs `curl` and `libuv1-dev`, as in the renv chapter.
  This project needs `libuv1-dev` because rmarkdown needs fs,
  through the packages bslib and sass.
  `git`, `less` and `nano` let you use Git, read files and edit files inside the container,
  `make` runs a `Makefile`,
  and `openssh-server` lets you log in to the container over ssh.
- The Quarto `RUN` line downloads Quarto 1.11.9 for your computer's processor,
  installs it, and deletes the download.
  `$(dpkg --print-architecture)` runs `dpkg --print-architecture`
  and puts what it prints, `amd64` or `arm64`, into the download address.
  Deleting the download in the same `RUN` line keeps it out of the image's layers
  (see [Building images](0630-containers-building.qmd)).
  Quarto makes PDFs with [Typst](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/typst.html),
  which comes with it, so the image does not need LaTeX.
- The line that adds `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` to `/etc/environment` is for ssh.
  `ENV` applies to the commands Docker starts in a container,
  but a session that logs in over ssh reads `/etc/environment` instead.
- `CMD ["/usr/sbin/sshd", "-D"]` makes a container run an ssh server when it starts,
  and `-D` keeps the server in the foreground, so the container keeps running.
  As in the earlier chapters, a command after the image name in `docker run` replaces it.
  [Docker Compose](0650-containers-docker-compose.qmd) starts this server,
  and a later chapter logs in to it.
- The commented-out `StrictModes no` line is for Linux computers,
  where the ssh server refuses a key file that the mount makes yours, not `root`'s.

The order follows [Building images](0630-containers-building.qmd).
The steps that rarely change, such as installing software, come first,
and the files that list packages are copied last,
so that adding a package rebuilds only the steps after its `COPY`.

:::{.exercise}

**Demonstration of container images being built from layers**

Let's follow the images that the docker-uv-renv image is built on:

- [docker-uv-renv's Dockerfile](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv/blob/main/Dockerfile)
- [rocker/r-ver:4.6.2's Dockerfile](https://github.com/rocker-org/rocker-versioned2/blob/master/dockerfiles/r-ver_4.6.2.Dockerfile)
- [The Ubuntu image on Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/_/ubuntu)

Questions:

1. What image does it build off?
2. What image does that build off?
3. And then the next one?
:::

## Build the image

From the project folder:

```bash
docker build --tag docker-uv-renv .
```

On a computer that has not built the image before, every step runs.
To show that here, the build below added `--no-cache`,
which runs every step again instead of reusing its layer.
The `FROM` steps still say `CACHED`,
because `--no-cache` does not download the base images again:

```bash
docker build --no-cache --tag docker-uv-renv .
```

The build took a little over two minutes.
`renv::restore()` took longest, then installing Quarto and the `apt-get` packages.
After this, a change to `pyproject.toml` or `renv.lock`
reruns only the steps from its `COPY` down.
The image is about 3 GB:

```bash
docker image ls docker-uv-renv
```

```out
IMAGE                   ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   EXTRA
docker-uv-renv:latest   80dad0100177       2.98GB          794MB        
```

## Use Python and R in one container

With the project folder mounted at `/workspace`,
the same container runs Python with uv:

::: {.panel-tabset group="shell"}
## macOS and Linux

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv-renv uv run python --version
```

## Windows (Git Bash)

```bash
docker run --rm -v "/$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv-renv uv run python --version
```

## Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/workspace" docker-uv-renv uv run python --version
```
:::

```out
Python 3.14.4
```

and R:

::: {.panel-tabset group="shell"}
## macOS and Linux

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv-renv Rscript -e 'R.version.string'
```

## Windows (Git Bash)

```bash
docker run --rm -v "/$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv-renv Rscript -e 'R.version.string'
```

## Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/workspace" docker-uv-renv Rscript -e 'R.version.string'
```
:::

```out
[1] "R version 4.6.2 (2026-10-29)"
```

## Render reports in both languages

`uv run quarto render` renders both reports.
`uv run` starts Quarto with the project's Python environment in `/opt/venv`,
so Quarto runs the Python code with the packages from `uv.lock`,
including `ipykernel` and `nbclient`, which Quarto needs to run Python code.
R finds the packages from `renv.lock` in `/opt/renv/library`,
because of the `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY` line:

::: {.panel-tabset group="shell"}
## macOS and Linux

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv-renv uv run quarto render
```

## Windows (Git Bash)

```bash
docker run --rm -v "/$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv-renv uv run quarto render
```

## Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/workspace" docker-uv-renv uv run quarto render
```
:::

Here are the main lines of the output, without the progress counters:

```out
[1/2] reports/report-python.qmd
Starting python3 kernel...[IPKernelApp] WARNING | Kernel is running over TCP without encryption. All communication (including code and outputs) is sent in plain text and is susceptible to eavesdropping. Use IPC transport or launch with kernel manager-provisioned CurveZMQ keys to enable transport encryption.
Done
Executing 'report-python.quarto_ipynb'
  Cell 1/2: ''...Done
  Cell 2/2: ''...Done
Starting python3 kernel...[IPKernelApp] WARNING | Kernel is running over TCP without encryption. All communication (including code and outputs) is sent in plain text and is susceptible to eavesdropping. Use IPC transport or launch with kernel manager-provisioned CurveZMQ keys to enable transport encryption.
Done
Executing 'report-python.quarto_ipynb'
  Cell 1/2: ''...Done
  Cell 2/2: ''...Done
[typst]: Compiling report-python.typ to report-python.pdf...DONE
[2/2] reports/report-r.qmd
processing file: report-r.qmd
output file: report-r.knit.md
processing file: report-r.qmd
output file: report-r.knit.md
[typst]: Compiling report-r.typ to report-r.pdf...DONE
Output created: reports/report-r.html
```

Quarto rendered each report twice,
once as HTML and once as a PDF with Typst,
because the project's `_quarto.yml` lists both formats.
The warning about TCP comes from the Python kernel that Quarto starts,
which talks to Quarto over a network connection inside the container.
Nothing leaves the container, so it does not matter here.

The reports are written to the mounted folder,
so they are in `reports/` on your computer:

```bash
ls reports
```

```out
report-python.html
report-python.pdf
report-python.qmd
report-r.html
report-r.pdf
report-r.qmd
```

[Docker Compose](0650-containers-docker-compose.qmd) shortens these `docker run` commands,
and the project's `Makefile` shortens them again,
to `make build` and `make render`.
